jobs.title: Senior Full Stack Engineer
jobs.description:
Ciklum is looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer to join our team in Argentina.
We are a custom product engineering company that supports both multinational organizations and scaling startups to solve their most complex business challenges. With a global team of over 4,000 highly skilled developers, consultants, analysts and product owners, we engineer technology that redefines industries and shapes the way people live.
About the role:
As a Senior Full Stack Engineer, you'll become a part of a cross-functional development team engineering experience of tomorrow.
Responsibilities:

- Hands-on Full Stack Development: Design, build, test, and maintain robust microservices and interactive user interfaces using PHP (Symfony) and Vue.js

- Autonomous Coverage & Ownership: Act as the primary technical point of contact during U.S./Canadian business hours, operating independently to maintain product stability and progress

- Client Engagement & Technical Onboarding: Partner closely with the Product Owner to support and onboard new clients, understanding their workflows and operational challenges

- Requirements Translation: Translate real-world client needs, feedback, and edge cases into actionable technical requirements, user stories, and architecture improvements

- Troubleshooting & Incident Resolution: Investigate, debug, and resolve high-priority technical issues and production defects promptly

- Continuous Improvement: Proactively identify opportunities to improve platform performance, code maintainability, testing coverage, and deployment processes

Requirements:

- Professional Experience: 5+ years of solid commercial software development experience across both backend and frontend domains

- Backend Expertise: Strong proficiency in modern PHP (8+) and hands-on experience with the Symfony framework designing and building RESTful APIs

- Frontend Skills: Proficient with modern JavaScript/TypeScript and hands-on experience building reactive client-facing applications or dashboards with Vue.js

- Architecture & Infrastructure: Solid understanding of microservice architectures and practical exposure to containerized environments with Kubernetes and Docker

- Client-Facing & Soft Skills: Excellent interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills in English; comfortable engaging directly with clients and cross-functional stakeholders

- Autonomy & Problem Solving: Demonstrated track record of working independently, managing multiple priorities, and troubleshooting complex technical issues without constant supervision

- Backend / API: PHP 8+, Symfony

- Frontend: Vue.js (Admin & Customer-facing Dashboards), HTML5, CSS3, modern JavaScript

- Architecture: Microservices, REST APIs

- Infrastructure & Orchestration: Kubernetes, Docker

What’s in it for you?

- Care: your mental and physical health is our priority. We ensure comprehensive company-paid medical insurance and mental health programs, 5 undocumented sick-leave days per year

- Tailored education path: boost your skills and knowledge with our regular internal events (meetups, conferences, workshops), Udemy license, language courses and company-paid certifications

- Growth environment: share your experience and level up your expertise with a community of skilled professionals, locally and globally

- Long-term employment with 20 working-days paid vacation and local bank holidays

- Flexibility: 100% remote work mode

- Opportunities: we value our specialists and always find the best options for them. Our Internal Mobility Program helps change a project if needed to help you grow, excel professionally and fulfill your potential

- Global impact: work on large-scale projects that redefine industries with international and fast-growing clients

- Welcoming environment: feel empowered with a friendly team, open-door policy, informal atmosphere within the company and regular team-building events

About us:
At Ciklum, we are always exploring innovations, empowering each other to achieve more, and engineering solutions that matter. With us, you’ll work with cutting-edge technologies, contribute to impactful projects, and be part of a One Team culture that values collaboration and progress.
As we expand into Latin America, every Ciklumer is helping to shape our story. Collaborate with seasoned experts and make a global impact backed by two decades of industry leadership.
Explore, empower, engineer with Ciklum!
Interested already? We would love to get to know you! Submit your application. We can’t wait to see you at Ciklum.

Company Overview
Our client sells subscription software to property managers. It has an iOS and Android app for field capture, a web dashboard for reports, tenant self-inspections and work orders. It grows through direct sales, referrals and partnerships, and it connects to the systems customers already use.
The CEO founded the company in California in 2014. It also turns voice notes into inspection reports with AI. The team is fully remote, and the engineering manager works from Uruguay.
Your Role
As Senior Software Engineer, you'll own features on the product engineering team, from the first product conversation through release and what happens in production afterwards. The seat is hands-on and covers Senior to Staff level. It's a full-time remote contractor role on Pacific time hours.
You'll report to the Head of Product Engineering and work closely with product. The team is building more with AI, and it's moving parts of its single large codebase into separate services while customers keep using the product. We prefer people based in Latin America whose day shares several hours with Pacific time.
Success means a feature you built is live and you're watching it in production. It also means you've fixed production data problems at the root cause, and your code reviews show in the work of the engineers around you.
You'll

- Own features from the first product conversation through release and fixes after launch

- Write short design notes and share them with the team before building

- Fix late, repeated or cut-off mobile uploads at their root cause

- Speed up queries over a dataset of 100M+ inspection photos

- Build AI features on the voice-to-report tool, with a safe fallback for wrong output

- Watch production after each release and fix what breaks

- Help decide which parts of the monolith become separate services, and in what order

- Review pull requests and mentor engineers, giving the reason for each comment

You Bring

- Several years building and running a live product where mistakes cost customers

- Full-stack experience with significant backend depth: services, data and APIs, plus React or Next.js and mobile work

- A product mindset: you start from the customer's problem and ask product sharp questions

- Features taken from rough idea to release, then watched in production

- A production problem you debugged to its root cause and can walk through

- AI tools in your engineering workflow every day, and AI-powered features you've shipped to real users

- Clear English, written and spoken, for design notes and pull requests

- Code review and mentoring of other engineers

- Self-starting habits that suit a small, remote team

Bonus Points

- Led a cross-team initiative or defined the architecture of a major system

- Moved part of a monolith into services while customers kept using the product

- Built offline capture or sync with retries and duplicate handling

What's Offered

- What we'd estimate for a role like this: $5,000 to $8,500 USD a month, based on experience. Share the range that fits your level and we'll go from there.

Interview Process
1️⃣ First call: 30 minutes with us at atomic✳HR on what you have built, working terms and what you want next.
2️⃣ Interviews with the engineering team: conversations about systems you have owned, what broke in them, how you found out and what you changed afterwards.
3️⃣ Final conversation with the CEO: on how you would work with product and the team, and what you would want to take on first.
4️⃣ Identity verification: a check that you are the person on the profile, done before an offer is made.
5️⃣ Offer: level, monthly rate in USD and start date, in writing.

About Crimson Education

Crimson Education is the world's leading college admissions consulting firm, with over 1,490 Ivy League offers and 2,410 to the US Top 15. We help ambitious students gain admission to the world's top universities through expert-led guidance and proven, data-driven strategies. We're backed by leading VC firms, recently closed a USD $40M Series D at a USD $640M valuation, and operate across 28 markets worldwide.
The Role
Crimson is replacing Salesforce with Salesflow, an AI-native CRM we build in-house. It runs the whole sales journey: lead intake, meeting scheduling, call transcription analysis, AI-drafted appraisals, contracts and e-signature, and invoicing. It is live for our US sales team today and rolls out to every other market over the coming months.
Our team is small and builder-heavy, and the rate of growth has made it hard to keep the underlying infrastructure and logic clean and tidy. As examples, CI checks things that have been fully deprecated, newly added modules do not always take into account legacy compatibility, and bug fixes are sometimes too narrow in scope, fixing the place the problem was seen and not the underlying cause. Compounding the above is that the code itself is for the most part written by AI – this is what enabled us to build a fully working CRM in a matter of months, but is what makes it very easy to inadvertently cross wires during development.
We are looking for the person who fixes this: you will own the backend view of the system as a whole and maintain the code that glues everything together. That means a system inventory and state transition models, CI that tests only what is needed and does that well, shared guarded entrypoints in place of multiple writers with inconsistent guards, and clear definitions for what is the source of truth when fields are shared among multiple synced systems. Salesflow is live and people depend on it every day, so this is done in steps while it runs: there is no rewrite. This is not a hands-off design role: you will be expected to push code as well as design.
In addition to the above, you'll also help to unblock users – the support team funnel tickets that prevent a user from working and require a backend code change to the dev team, most of whom are not in US time zones. You will join the team and cover the US working day, when the other members are offline.
We fully expect you to use AI to augment your analyses and write code for you but absolutely require that you have the experience to read and write code yourself, and that you know how to use AI to write code (e.g., which questions to ask, what to check, how to build internal memory structures).
What are the main responsibilities for this role?
Your top priority is to build and maintain the view of the CRM as a whole: inventory all functions, edge functions, flows, and integrations with outside systems; build the state transition map and the set of business rules the system is held to; and then ensure that architecture and CI align to this. In practice this can be split into:

- setting up a live and auto-updating inventory and model: the repo has multiple pushes every day; no-one should try updating a model by hand

- coordinating with team members on business rules: the team has, collectively, all the info; your job is to organize it and embed it in the checks

- after the above two, move into implementation: resolve technical debt caused by rapid organic growth without consistent pruning, and set up the infrastructure such that future growth automatically falls into the correct path and does not create new debt.

Aside from this, you will assist in unblocking users during US daytime hours: addressing current bugs will help you gain insight into the system as a whole, informing the main priority.

- Your first 14 days: inventory and build a model of the system; integrate into the ticket queue

- Your first 28 days: start shipping basic sanitation: clean CI and updated CLAUDE.md files (the instructions our AI agents read) so future pushes don't create more problems

- Your first 3 months: the worst of the debt is cleared and guardrails are in place, so a bug that has been fixed does not come back; your time will transition over to building new features

What skills and experience are required?
You think in systems. Shown a new product, you look for the states, the transitions and the rules that must always hold before you look at the code. You can draw how it works on one page, and you can predict from that drawing where it will break.
